Chapter 03 of 19

The Crows

CommuteEast Van / eastward routes90 BPM
The story

Every morning the crows leave their roost in Burnaby and cross East Vancouver in one long, loose formation. Every evening they fly back, on time, like a shift change at a factory. That is exactly what it is. The crows are the workforce of Terminal City: organized, punctual, and not especially polite.

Their job is inspection. They check the Wire Choir line by line, listening for anything that has fallen out of tune. When a crow finds a fault, it does not write a report. It lands on it. A crow standing perfectly still on a wire is a work order, and the Repair People will come to fix whatever the crow is standing on. Nobody assigns the crows this work. They simply do it.

The crows take their shift from the Morning Mist and hand the city over to the Nocturnals when they go home. Without them the city would never know it was broken until something stopped working. Clock in. Black on the line. They count the faults on their way home.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
